title: Lyapunov/Sylvester solver as Kronecker-sum inversion; Gramian as Van Loan integral
expression_sketch:
Sylvester equation A*X + X*B = C (A in C**(n,n), B in C**(m,m), X, C in C**(n,m)). Vectorization identity:
  vec(A*X + X*B) = (kron(I_m, A) + kron(B.T, I_n)) * vec(X).
Real Lyapunov A*X + X*A.T = Q (Q = Q.T):
  (kron(I, A) + kron(A, I)) * vec(X) = vec(Q).
Unique solution iff spec(A) intersect spec(-B) is empty (Lyapunov: lam_i(A) + lam_j(A) != 0 for all i, j).
If additionally Re(lam_i(A)) < 0 for all i and Q = Q.T, the unique solution is the Gramian integral
  X = Integral(exp(t*A)*Q*exp(t*A.T), (t, 0, oo)).
Van Loan: that integral is a block of the exponential of a block-triangular matrix built from A and Q.
1x1 SymPy member: 2*a*x = q, x = q/(2*a) for a != 0.
Differentiated Lyapunov (sensitivity): dA*X + A*dX + dX*A.T + X*dA.T = dQ, so dX solves another Lyapunov equation with the same Kronecker-sum operator.
latent_structure: Master linear operator: the Kronecker sum I⊗A + A⊗I (Lyapunov) / I⊗A + B^T⊗I (Sylvester). The algebraic solver, the infinite-horizon Gramian integral, the Van Loan block exponential, and the sensitivity equation for dX are four members of that one operator. Autodiff through a Lyapunov/Gramian solver is inversion of the same master, not a new fit.

why_not_cse_lgg: Expanded n^2 scalar equations of A X + X A.T = Q look like a generic linear system. CSE will not pack them as (I⊗A+A⊗I) vec(X). LGG will not identify the Gramian integral and the algebraic solver as instances of one Kronecker-sum master, nor see that autodiff of the solver reuses that operator. This is an operator-level representation, not CSE.
